classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied subdivision and explicit congruence instruction to select triangles ABM and ACM, translate midpoint into equal sides, recognise AM as common, and apply SSS followed by corresponding-angle equality.

content.prompt:
In the diagram to the right, $ABC$ is isosceles with $AB=AC$ and $M$ is the midpoint of the interval $BC$. Prove that $\angle ABC=\angle ACB$.

(Only congruence is to be used.)

spec.description: Triangle ABC with apex A, horizontal base BC, midpoint M and segment AM. No equality ticks or right-angle marker. Ordinary source blue is rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: The text supplies AB=AC and BM=MC; the diagram supplies the subdivision into triangles ABM and ACM.
spec.answerVisibility: No derived equal angles or perpendicularity are shown.

answer.short: $\triangle ABM\equiv\triangle ACM$ (SSS). Hence $\angle ABC=\angle ACB$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).
answer.worked:
In triangles $ABM$ and $ACM$:
$$\begin{align*}AB&=AC &&\text{(given)}\\BM&=CM &&\text{(}M\text{ is the midpoint of }BC\text{)}\\AM&=AM &&\text{(common side).}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle ABM\equiv\triangle ACM$ (SSS), so $\angle ABM=\angle ACM$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).

Since $B$, $M$ and $C$ are collinear, $\angle ABC=\angle ACB$.
